free_tier.stated: Free: 5 GB of pooled Object Storage and IPFS storage, 500 pinned files, 10 GB a month of IPFS egress and free object egress; Pro $7.50 a month raises storage to 500 GB
free_tier.notes: the pricing page was read on 2026-11-01; the binding constraint is the 5 GB volume, which limits[] carries

per_object_cap.stated: the pricing page states no per-object cap; the limits it does state are a bucket count and a pinned-file count

retention.stated: Pinned content stays on the Filebase node indefinitely and files uploaded to an IPFS bucket stay pinned for as long as they are kept in the bucket; the pricing page states no period, its footnote calling pinned files objects maintained for persistence on the IPFS network
retention.notes: indefinite while the file is pinned and kept in the bucket; deleting an object unpins the CID and Filebase stops guaranteeing its availability; the pricing page's footnote describes pinning as persistence with no period

egress.terms: Split, and the split is the trap. 'For S3-compatible object storage buckets on the non-IPFS tier at s3.filebase.io, egress is free on every paid plan.' But 'IPFS bandwidth is not free... On the free tier, there is a 5 GB / month egress cap' — and the pricing page states 10 GB IPFS Egress. Either way it is single-digit-to-10 GB/month.
egress.free_allowance: 10 GB per month of IPFS egress on Free

tooling: S3 API at s3.filebase.io, region 'auto', SigV4; rclone s3 backend works; IPFS Pinning Service API; dedicated gateways; docs list rclone/boto3/aws-cli explicitly.
chaining: 1 bucket on Free, no limit on object count within it. 5 GB per account is not repeatable to 500 GB in any practical way, and each account needs its own S3 keys.

limits.value: 5 GB of pooled storage on the Free plan

limits_note: Single PUT 5 GB; multipart total 5 TB (1 TB recommended); 500 req/s S3 API; 1 bucket on Free; 500 pinned files.

identity_cost.detail: the sign-up form asks for a first name, a last name, an email address and a password, with a Google sign-up option; no card, phone or ID field appears on the form

reliability_note: S3 API held up live: the public gateway served the test CID at 200 (414,201 bytes, Server: Filebase) but throttled during a rapid burst (2 of 8 answered before the burst ran long). The 'no egress fees' headline applies to the S3 tier, not the IPFS tier — a genuinely confusing pricing page and the single most common misread in this niche.
